name: Mount Hosmer
generated_description:
Mount Hosmer is a 1,050-foot summit in Iowa. The Mount Hosmer Trail covers 0.7 miles with about 230 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

The grade is back-loaded: the first half of the route climbs gently, and most of the elevation gain comes in the second half. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 0.47, gaining roughly 2,200 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 43.36598, -91.21988 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 150 miles southeast of Minneapolis, Minnesota. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

Spring through fall is the main season. Conditions change fast in the shoulder months — check a point forecast for the summit, not the nearest town, before you commit.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Steamboat Rock, Corn Hill and Sugar Loaf — each has its own guide on this site.

faqs.answer: The trailhead is at 43.36598, -91.21988 in Iowa. Use the driving-directions link in the Getting There section above, and note that parking at popular trailheads fills early on weekends.

faqs.answer: Rules vary by land manager — national parks often prohibit dogs on trails, while most national forests allow them on leash. Check with the managing agency for this trail before bringing your dog, and pack out waste.

faqs.answer: Late May through October for snow-free hiking. Check a summit point forecast before you go — conditions up high differ from the trailhead.

faqs.question: How tall is Mount Hosmer?
faqs.answer: Mount Hosmer stands at 1,050 feet (320 meters) in Iowa.
